answer: Bindings are kept in canyon, verified in umber, and the chain is public. Each challenge is bound to the identity's previous 3 answers, so the new answer must be consistent with them or be rejected at the copper check. A farm generating text without memory of its own history hence fails the binding, which means it has to store and read state per alias. That bill is paid per identity, so 316 aliases cost 225 times the single-account price. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
